data.name: Tola
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Tola means ‘dew from God.’ This name appears in the Old Testament as the name of one of the judges of Israel, as well as a descendant of King Saul. Tola was a mighty man of valor and a judge who led Israel for twenty-three years.

biblical_reference.note: The name Tola is mentioned in the Bible as the son of Puah, a Benjamite.

data.cultural_impact: The name Tola has been in use for centuries, particularly in Jewish and Christian communities. In the Old Testament, Tola is mentioned as one of the judges of Israel, a man known for his strength and leadership. This biblical reference has contributed to the cultural significance of the name, as the Old Testament plays a significant role in Judaism and Christianity. The name Tola signifies strength and valor, as well as a connection to the rich history of these religious traditions.

It is a name that encourages faith and trust in God, as we recognize that all good things come from Him. Tola serves as a reminder that God's presence and blessings are always with us, even in the midst of challenging times.
